title: Coherence of exceptional fibre comparisons for section families
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\geq1$ with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be Noetherian with $N$ invertible on $S$. Work in the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse images. For every compactifiable structural map $b$ write $\omega_b=b^\times A$ using the right adjoint of $Rb_!$. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes d}$, with $A_T(0)=A_T$.
Let $d\geq0$ and $q:D\to X=\mathbf A^1_S$ be smooth separated compactifiable of pure relative dimension $d$, with $D$ Noetherian and a closed section $\sigma$. Let $(g:V\to S,s)$ and $(\pi:E\to S,z)$ be its Cartesian pairs at $1$ and $0$. Write $a:X\to S$, $C=s^*\omega_g$, $F=\sigma^*\omega_q$, $H=z^*\omega_\pi$, and let $\theta:i_1^*F\to C$, $\eta:i_0^*F\to H$ be the exceptional base-change isomorphisms obtained by transposing the pulled-back counit through inverse compact-support exchange.
For any $v:S'\to S$ of Noetherian schemes, let primes denote the base-changed diagram, $\bar v:\mathbf A^1_{S'}\to X$, and suppose all structural maps used are compactifiable. Let $b_C:v^*C\to C'$, $b_F:\bar v^*F\to F'$, and $b_H:v^*H\to H'$ be the section pullbacks of those same counit-defined exceptional comparisons. They are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$\theta'\,i_1'^*b_F=b_C\,v^*\theta,\qquad\eta'\,i_0'^*b_F=b_H\,v^*\eta.$$
For successive changes of base the structural comparison satisfies $b_{vw}=b'_w\circ w^*b_v$, with all inverse-image compositors inserted.
Likewise let $h_D:D_1\to D$ be a separated etale finite-type map over $X$ between such families, carrying their sections to one another, with Cartesian squares of centres and induced maps $h_V:V_1\to V$, $h_E:E_1\to E$ on the two fibres. Assume the sources are Noetherian and all structural maps and composites used are compactifiable. Let $b_C:C\to C_1$, $b_F:F\to F_1$, $b_H:H\to H_1$ be the isomorphisms from etale adjoint locality, normalized by the composite adjunction counits. Then
$$\theta_1 i_1^*b_F=b_C\theta,\qquad\eta_1 i_0^*b_F=b_H\eta.$$
These identities concern the specified maps, not just existence of abstract fibre isomorphisms.
If these families have unique isomorphisms $\kappa:F\to a^*C$ normalized by $\theta$ (and the corresponding primed or subscript-$1$ isomorphisms), the same specified maps satisfy
$$\kappa'=a'^*b_C\circ\bar v^*\kappa\circ b_F^{-1},\qquad\delta' b_C=b_H v^*\delta,$$
where $\delta=\eta\circ(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}$ and likewise for $\delta'$. For the etale-family map they satisfy $\kappa_1=a^*b_C\circ\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}$ and $\delta_1 b_C=b_H\delta$.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product], [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Gluing, coherence of counit-defined fibre maps under arbitrary base change and etale locality; old item Steps 12–14.

proof.text:
Write $P_f=Rf_!\dashv G_f=f^\times$, with counit $\epsilon_f$, and $C_{f,v}:v^*P_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f'}r^*$ for compact-support exchange, where $r$ is the upper arrow. Put $\beta_{f,v,K}:r^*G_fK\to G_{f'}v^*K$. Its defining equation is
$$\epsilon_{f',v^*K}\circ P_{f'}(\beta_{f,v,K})=v^*\epsilon_{f,K}\circ C_{f,v,G_fK}^{-1}.$$
At $K=A$ insert $v^*A\cong A$; section pullback gives exactly the maps in the statement. All structural sources, including the primed fibres, are Noetherian by finite type over the Noetherian base; $X$ and $X'$ are affine lines over those bases. Smooth relative dimension is preserved by base change, so the smooth exceptional-base-change theorem applies to $q,g,\pi$ and all their base changes: finite $A$, $NA=0$, invertible $N$, Noetherian schemes, and compactifiable separated structural maps are precisely the hypotheses here. It makes $b_C,b_F,b_H,\theta,\eta$ isomorphisms. Throughout the proof use the canonical inverse-image compositors and constant-unit comparisons; their associativity and unit compatibility are those of the cited unbounded pullback-composition lemma.

source.place: Opening paragraph (fibre restrictions); ordinary-etale formulation via prop-asd-smooth-base-change

proof.text:
For successive base changes $v:B'\to B$, $w:B''\to B'$, write $r,r'$ for the upper arrows and $f',f''$ for the structural maps. Compact-support pasting says
$$C_{f,vw}=C_{f',w,r^*(-)}\circ w^*C_{f,v}.$$
Apply the mate-pasting identity (1) to the inverse exchanges, with left adjoints $P_f,P_{f'},P_{f''}$ and right adjoints $G_f,G_{f'},G_{f''}$. It gives, naturally in $K$,
$$\beta_{f,vw,K}=\beta_{f',w,v^*K}\circ r'^*\beta_{f,v,K}.$$
This is an equality of the counit-defined maps of Step 1, not a choice of isomorphisms. At $K=A$, the pullback-unit coherence removes the intermediate $v^*A$; pulling back by compatible sections gives $b_{vw}=b'_w\circ w^*b_v$.

source.place: Tag 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek), compatibility with composite base changes; mateEquiv_vcomp

proof.text: For $t=0,1$ put $q_t:D_t\to S$ and $\sigma_t:S\to D_t$. The two paths from $S'$ to $X$ are $i_t\circ v$ and $\bar v\circ i_t'$. Their pullback diagrams have the same outer rectangle. Step 2 applied to the first factorization gives $\beta_{q_t,v}\circ r_t^*\beta_{q,i_t}$; applied to the second gives $\beta_{q',i_t'}\circ j_t'^*\beta_{q,\bar v}$. Both are $\beta$ of that rectangle. Pull this equality back by $\sigma_t'$ and use the section equalities. For $t=1$ it reads $\theta'\circ i_1'^*b_F=b_C\circ v^*\theta$; for $t=0$ it reads $\eta'\circ i_0'^*b_F=b_H\circ v^*\eta$.

source.place: Opening fibre restrictions and Gluing; apply the preceding transitivity equation to the two factorizations

proof.text:
Here is the normalization needed for the etale-family maps. For a separated etale finite-type $e:T_1\to T$ over $B$, put $f_1=fe$, $E=De_{\Sigma!}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_e:Ee^*\to1$. The graph-normalized comparison identifies $P_e$ with $E$, so compact-support composition supplies $\alpha:P_fE\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f_1}$. The locality isomorphism $\lambda_{e,K}:e^*G_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f_1}K$ is characterized by
$$\epsilon_{f_1,K}\circ P_{f_1}(\lambda_{e,K})=\epsilon_{f,K}\circ P_f(\operatorname{ev}_{e,G_fK})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{e^*G_fK}=:t_K.$$
Indeed the right side is exactly the composite-adjunction counit for $P_fE\dashv e^*G_f$, transported through $\alpha$. Thus this equation specifies the locality map in the question, including its counit normalization. No claim about the mate of an arbitrary isomorphism being invertible is used: invertibility comes from etale adjoint locality and adjunction-preserving right-adjoint uniqueness.

source.place: Second paragraph: the three Hom bijections and compatibility with counits

proof.text:
Base change $e$ along $r:T'\to T$ to $e':T_1'\to T'$, with upper arrow $r_1$ and square identification $\vartheta:r_1^*e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}e'^*r^*$. Let $\beta:E'r_1^*\to r^*E$ be the specified sum-extension comparison, invertible by the etale-shriek base-change lemma, and $B_e=\beta^{-1}$. On module sheaves we show
$$r^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,M}\circ\beta_{e^*M}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',r^*M}\circ E'(\vartheta_M),$$
that is, $r^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,M}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',r^*M}\circ B_{e,e^*M}$ with $\vartheta$ inserted. Compare transposes under the composite adjunction $L_2=E'r_1^*\dashv R_2=r_{1*}e'^*$, with $L_1=r^*E\dashv R_1=e^*r_*$. By its definition, the transpose of $\beta_X$ is $\operatorname{Ex}^0_{L_1X}\circ\eta_{1,X}$. Naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}^0$ and the triangle identity $e^*\operatorname{ev}_e\circ\eta_{e,e^*M}=1$ turn the transpose of the left side into $\operatorname{Ex}^0_{r^*M}\circ e^*\eta_{r,M}$. Expanding $\operatorname{Ex}^0$ as the transpose of $e'^*\varepsilon_r\circ\vartheta_{r_*}$, naturality of $\vartheta$ and the triangle identity of $r^*\dashv r_*$ make this $r_{1*}(\vartheta_M)\circ\eta_{r_1,e^*M}$. By the triangle identity of $E'\dashv e'^*$, the transpose of the right side is the same map. Exactness of sum extension and inverse image gives the equality term by term on every complex, and then in the unbounded derived category, where the counit of $DE\dashv e^*$ is termwise evaluation. The graph-normalization theorem identifies this $B_e$ with compact-support exchange for $e$, including its sum/evaluation adjunction; thus the calculation applies to the specified compactification maps.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change): the comparison of left adjoints obtained from the right adjoints; counit calculation by transposition

proof.text:
Retain $e,f$ of Step 4, base-change the whole diagram along $v:B'\to B$, and use primed notation. Compatibility of compact exchange with composition and its graph normalization give
$$C_{f_1,v}\circ v^*\alpha=\alpha'\circ P_{f'}(B_e)\circ C_{f,v,E(-)}.$$
Take transposes under $P_{f_1'}\dashv G_{f_1'}$ of the two maps
$$\lambda_{e',v^*K}\circ e'^*\beta_{f,v,K},\qquad
\beta_{f_1,v,K}\circ r_1^*\lambda_{e,K}.$$
For the second map, naturality of $C_{f_1,v}^{-1}$ and Step 1 give $v^*t_K\circ C_{f_1,v,e^*G_fK}^{-1}$. For the first map substitute Step 4's composite counit, move $\beta_{f,v,K}$ across $\operatorname{ev}_{e'}$ by naturality, and substitute Step 1's transpose. Replace $\alpha'^{-1}C_{f_1,v}$ using the displayed composition equation, and replace $\operatorname{ev}_{e'}B_e$ by Step 5. The result is again $v^*t_K\circ C_{f_1,v,e^*G_fK}^{-1}$. The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so
$$\lambda_{e',v^*K}\circ e'^*\beta_{f,v,K}=\beta_{f_1,v,K}\circ r_1^*\lambda_{e,K}.$$
The cited mate-pasting rules (2),(3) are precisely these substitutions for a composite adjunction and its conjugate; all inverse-image compositors are inserted as in Step 1.

source.place: Tags 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek), composition/base-change compatibility; composite-adjunction mate calculation

proof.text: Apply Step 6 with $f=q$, $e=h_D$, and $v=i_t$ for each $t=0,1$. Their base-changed etale maps are exactly $h_V$ and $h_E$. Evaluate at the constant object and pull back by the sections on the source family. Because the sections are carried to one another, $\sigma_1^*h_D^*=\sigma^*$, and likewise on the two fibres. Consequently the pulled-back locality maps are exactly $b_F,b_C,b_H$ of the question; Step 4 and etale locality make them isomorphisms. For $t=1$ the resulting equation is $\theta_1\circ i_1^*b_F=b_C\circ\theta$, and for $t=0$ it is $\eta_1\circ i_0^*b_F=b_H\circ\eta$.

source.place: Local construction and Gluing: etale maps of pairs, fibre identifications, and normalized comparison

proof.text:
Assume the unique normalized isomorphisms in the last paragraph of the statement exist. For base change define
$$\widetilde\kappa=a'^*b_C\circ\bar v^*\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}:F'\xrightarrow{\sim}a'^*C'.$$
The canonical comparison $\bar v^*a^*\cong a'^*v^*$ is inserted. On the unit section its restriction is
$$i_1'^*\widetilde\kappa=b_C\circ v^*\theta\circ(i_1'^*b_F)^{-1}=\theta'$$
by Step 3. Hence $\widetilde\kappa$ satisfies the required normalization, and uniqueness for the primed family forces $\kappa'=\widetilde\kappa$. This uses uniqueness only after constructing an isomorphism with the prescribed restriction; it assumes no full faithfulness of affine-line pullback.

source.place: Gluing: uniqueness of the isomorphism normalized at t=1; its application to a base-changed family

proof.text:
Restrict Step 8 to the zero section, where $i_0'^*a'^*$ is the identity up to the canonical unit. Invert the resulting equality to obtain
$$(i_0'^*\kappa')^{-1}\circ b_C=i_0'^*b_F\circ v^*(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}.$$
Compose with $\eta'$ on the left and apply Step 3 at $t=0$. The result is
$$\delta'\circ b_C=\eta'\circ i_0'^*b_F\circ v^*(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}=b_H\circ v^*\eta\circ v^*(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}=b_H\circ v^*\delta.$$
All factors have source $v^*C$ and target $H'$ after the indicated compositions.

source.place: Last paragraph: restrict the normalized comparison to t=0 and take its inverse

proof.text: For the etale-family map define $\widetilde\kappa_1=a^*b_C\circ\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}$. Step 7 at $t=1$ gives $i_1^*\widetilde\kappa_1=b_C\theta(i_1^*b_F)^{-1}=\theta_1$, so uniqueness implies $\kappa_1=\widetilde\kappa_1$. At $t=0$ its inverse gives $(i_0^*\kappa_1)^{-1}b_C=i_0^*b_F(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1}$. Compose with $\eta_1$ and use Step 7 at zero to get $\delta_1b_C=b_H\delta$. This proves both remaining identities for exactly the counit-normalized etale comparisons.

source.place: Local construction and Gluing: uniqueness under etale maps of pairs and zero-fibre specialization
